mean.def: The sum of the values divided by how many there are: $\bar{x} = \frac{\sum x_i}{n}$ for a sample. It is not resistant.

population-mean.def: The mean of a whole population, written $\mu$ (mu). It is a parameter, estimated by the sample mean $\bar{x}$.

median.def: The middle value of the ordered data, or the average of the two middle values when n is even. Half the data are at or below it. It is resistant.

quartile.def: The first quartile $Q_1$ is the median of the lower half of the ordered data and the third quartile $Q_3$ is the median of the upper half (the median itself is left out of both halves when n is odd).

percentile.def: The pth percentile is the value with p percent of the data at or below it.

range.def: The maximum minus the minimum: a single number that measures spread. It is not resistant.

iqr.def: The interquartile range, $\text{IQR} = Q_3 - Q_1$: the spread of the middle half of the data. It is resistant.

standard-deviation.def: A measure of the typical distance of the values from the mean: $s = \sqrt{\frac{\sum (x_i - \bar{x})^2}{n - 1}}$ for a sample. It is 0 only when every value is the same, and it is not resistant.

variance.def: The square of the standard deviation, $s^2 = \frac{\sum (x_i - \bar{x})^2}{n - 1}$ for a sample.

population-sd.def: The standard deviation of a whole population, written $\sigma$ (sigma). It is a parameter, estimated by the sample standard deviation $s$.

outlier-rule.def: A value is an outlier if it is below $Q_1 - 1.5 \times \text{IQR}$ or above $Q_3 + 1.5 \times \text{IQR}$ (the fences). Another rule flags values more than 2 standard deviations from the mean.

resistant.def: A summary is resistant if extreme values barely change it. The median and IQR are resistant; the mean, standard deviation and range are not.
